2010_008_081710regmtg.paragraph: Troy School District's Board of Education met in regular session on Tuesday, August 17, 2010 at 7:00 p.m. in the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan, with Superintendent Barbara A. Fowler, Ph.D. and Assistant Superintendent for Business Services Mark S. Rajter. The packet is dominated by the June and July 2010 Treasurer's Reports — full Pentamation check registers, ACH debit and wire-transfer schedules, and fund-level budget-to-actual statements showing a June 30, 2010 General Fund balance of $12,510,272 — together with action items awarding a diesel fuel contract extension to RKA Petroleum Company not to exceed $330,000.00 and infrared classroom microphones to VSC, Inc. for $74,641.00.

**Meeting**
Troy School District (City of Troy, County of Oakland, Michigan) Board of Education regular meeting, Tuesday, August 17, 2010, 7:00 p.m., Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 58 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW). Board members named: Underwood (President), Miletti (Vice President), Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Philippart, Pochodylo.

**Recognition**
Mr. Jolly read biographies of 27 spring-sport All-State athletes, including synchronized swimmers coached by Lori Uchwal, girls track athletes coached by Matt Richardson, girls lacrosse under Elizabeth Waters, softball under Tom Calnen, girls soccer under Brian Zawislak, water polo under Lucas Ortego, and boys track under Eric Prowse. Most attend Troy High School; Amanda Sliney attends Athens High School and Kaylin Youn the International Academy.

**Consent agenda (item 5)**
Minutes of the July 13, 2010 meeting (resolutions 10-069 through 10-080, each carried 6-0 with Miletti absent), the Treasurer's Reports for June and July 2010, and the diesel fuel bid award. The July minutes awarded elementary science kits to Delta Education ($138,280.00), playground surface materials to Rolar Property Services ($74,340.00), and radio frequency microphones to Videotape Products, Inc. ($24,623.05), all from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund; enrolled six secondary schools in the MHSAA for August 1, 2010 through July 31, 2011; named Mark S. Rajter Board Treasurer for July through December 2010; and went into closed session on negotiations at 7:40 p.m., reconvening at 9:07 p.m. and adjourning at 9:08 p.m.

June YTD, FY2010: General Fund $12,510,272 at June 30, 2010 (from $14,984,549 on July 1, 2009), with revenue of $135,916,301 against expenditures of $137,649,866 and excess revenue over expenditures of (2,474,277). A footnote states the budget-resolution Special Revenue fund balance of $7,639,053 "included $5,610,166 Durant fund balance that beginning 2010-2011 is part of General Fund," leaving $2,028,887. **Action items**
5.C — Diesel fuel contract extended to RKA Petroleum Company, not to exceed $330,000.00 from the 2010-11 General Fund; Bid Award #9147; estimated annual usage 160,000 gallons; total 2009/10 diesel cost was $268,119.
6.A — Probationary contracts for Kathy Cappuso, Angela DeClerck, Courtney Fix, James Kurecka, Eileen Rabourn, Nanette Renkiewicz and Jennifer Royston.
6.B/6.C — Resignation of Tim McAvoy, Director of Community Relations, effective August 9, 2010; appointment of Kerry Birmingham as Director of Community & Media Relations effective August 23, 2010 on a two-year probationary administrative contract.
7.A — Schools of Choice under Section 105c for 2011-2012: ten non-resident 10th graders and an unlimited number of 9th graders at the International Academy East.
8.A — Infrared wireless microphones to VSC, Inc., $74,641.00, from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund (Bid #9687).
8.B — Sidewalk easement at Wattles Elementary School from Satyendra N. Basu and Indira Basu, 553 Colebrook.
10.A-10.C — 2010/11 board committee assignments; cancelation of the September 23-24, 2010 fall retreat; a special workshop on September 28, 2010 at 6:00 p.m.
11.A — Closed session on negotiations under Public Act 267, Section 8(c).

**Identity and meeting.** Troy School District, a K-12 local district in the City of Troy, County of Oakland, Michigan, at 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098 (248.823.4000; www.troy.k12.mi.us), held a Board of Education regular meeting on Tuesday, August 17, 2010 at 7:00 p.m. in the Administration Building. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 58 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. except in July and August. The agenda ran: pledge of allegiance; recognition of spring All-State athletes; additions and deletions; public communication; general consent agenda (July 13, 2010 minutes; Treasurer's Report for June and July 2010; bid award for diesel fuel); personnel (elementary and secondary hires, administrative resignation, appointment of a Director of Community and Media Relations); curriculum (Schools of Choice, Section 105c); business (infrared classroom microphones; sidewalk easement at Wattles Elementary School); other (2010/2011 board committee assignments; cancelation of the September 23-24, 2010 fall retreat; scheduling a special workshop for September 28, 2010); closed session on negotiations; adjournment.

**Recognition.** Twenty-seven 2010 spring All-State athletes were named, with Mr. Jolly reading each biography: Merna Abdou, Francesca Adamski, Jessica Benton, Skylar Darish, Katie Dunn, Sara Dykowski, Emily Dzik, Samantha Johnson, Vivien Lee, Sophie Li, Jennifer Liu, Lindsey Miller, Michelle Moriset, Emily Muma, Monique Nguyen, Emily Raymond, Amanda Sliney (Athens High School), Kristen Soreide, Victoria Troccoli, Jordan Wheatley, Madeline Wideman, Annie Xiao, James Yau, Kaylin Youn (International Academy), Anna Young, Emily Young and Carlie Zitkus. Coaches credited include Lori Uchwal (synchronized swim), Matt Richardson (girls track), Elizabeth Waters (girls lacrosse), Tom Calnen (softball), Brian Zawislak (girls soccer), Lucas Ortego (girls water polo) and Eric Prowse (boys track).

**July 13, 2010 minutes (item 5.A).** President Underwood called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. at the Services Building with Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Philippart and Pochodylo present, Vice President Miletti absent, Superintendent Fowler and administrators Bryan, Keeling, Machesky, McAvoy, Rajter, Stromayer and Witt in attendance, plus four members of the audience; Nancy L. Philippart signed as Secretary. Resolutions 10-069 through 10-080 all carried Yes 6 / No 0 / Absent Miletti: the consent agenda (minutes of June 1, the June 8 special workshop and June 15, plus a copy paper bid award); an MHSAA membership resolution enrolling the district's six secondary schools for August 1, 2010 through July 31, 2011; a Schools of Choice resolution under Section 105c of the State School Aid Act of 1979 as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996 for 2010-2011 nonresident students attending the International Academy East from districts in another county whose intermediate school district is contiguous with the Oakland Intermediate School District; elementary science kits to Delta Education for $138,280.00; playground surface materials to Rolar Property Services for $74,340.00; radio frequency microphone equipment to Videotape Products, Inc. for $24,623.05 (all three expenditures of the 2004 Capital Projects Fund); naming Mark S. Rajter Director and Patricia Orczykowski Alternate Director to the MAISL Joint Risk Management Trust; appointing Mark S. Rajter Treasurer of the Board for July through December 2010; adopting the fund depositories and investment resolution for the same period; declaring intent to continue summer tax collections for the 2011-2012 fiscal year with notice to the City of Troy; scheduling a special workshop for August 17, 2010 at 5:30 p.m.; and going into closed session on negotiations under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), on a 6-0 roll call at 7:40 p.m., reconvening at 9:07 p.m. and adjourning at 9:08 p.m. Comments recorded: Shelly Carrier, Executive Secretary to the Superintendent, retired effective July 31, 2010 after 24 years of service; Dr. Fowler distributed the Budget Salary/Compensation Transparency Report required by the amended State School Aid Act to be posted within 30 days of budget adoption, with posting set for Thursday, July 15, 2010; over thirty bond projects were in progress; and Ms. Philippart asked about 20j funding, with Senator Papageorge having secured School Aid Bill language restoring 50% of 20j contingent on the Tax Amnesty Act, which the governor vetoed, the legality of vetoing boilerplate language then under review.

**Item 5.C — Diesel fuel.** The Board first approved a diesel fuel contract on June 15, 2004 for the 2004-05 year; in July 2010 RKA Petroleum Company asked to extend it through June 30, 2011 on the same terms, based on the lowest profit margin per gallon fixed for the contract period. The resolution extends the contract to RKA Petroleum Company in an amount not to exceed $330,000.00 as an expenditure of the 2010-11 General Fund. A memorandum of August 11, 2010 from Frank E. Lams, Supervisor, Purchasing and Budget (Purchasing Department, 1140 Rankin, Troy, MI 48083; 248-823-4052; fax 248-823-4077; flams2@troy.k12.mi.us) to Mark S. Rajter, referencing Bid Award #9147, states the cost per gallon per delivery/profit is $0.0045 for regular diesel versus $0.0147 for the Macomb/Oakland Fuel Consortium, estimates annual usage at 160,000 gallons, notes district pricing is grandfathered under the old contract, and records that "our total cost for diesel fuel in 2009/10 was $268,119." RKA's own letter of July 9, 2010, signed by Executive Vice President Keith Albertie (corporate office 28340 Wick Road, Romulus, MI 48174; operations office 28340 Goddard Road; (734) 946-2199), says the extension would run "up to July 31, 2011," describes the RKA companies as certified minority businesses (WBE), and notes RKA is a certified BQ9000 Biodiesel Distributer under the National Biodiesel Board.

**Items 6.A-6.C — Personnel.** Probationary contracts for 2010-2011 were recommended for Kathy Cappuso, 1.0 FTE ASD Teacher at Athens High School (B.A., Wayne State University, May 1997; Michigan Provisional Certificate May 2010; Shelby Township); Angela DeClerck, 1.0 Speech and Language Pathologist (M.A., Bowling Green State University, May 2010; B.A., Central Michigan University, May 2008; Ortonville); Courtney Fix, 1.0 Resource Room Teacher at Boulan Park Middle School (M.A., Aquinas College, December 2009; B.A., Michigan State University, May 2001; Rochester Hills); James Kurecka, .42 FTE Math Teacher at International Academy East (B.A., University of Michigan, August 2008; Rochester Hills); Eileen Rabourn, 1.0 FTE History Teacher at International Academy Central (M.A., Eastern Michigan University, August 2000; B.A., Michigan State University, March 1992; South Lyon); Nanette Renkiewicz, 0.9 FTE School Psychologist (M.A., University of Detroit Mercy, May 1999; B.A., Wayne State University, December 1988; Hamtramck); and Jennifer Royston, .67 FTE English/Speech Teacher at International Academy East (M.A., University College London, November 2009; B.A., Eastern Michigan University, December 2007; Monroe). The Board accepted with appreciation the resignation of Tim McAvoy, Director of Community Relations, hired November 27, 2000, effective August 9, 2010, and appointed Kerry Birmingham as Director of Community & Media Relations effective August 23, 2010 on a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure; she had spent two years as a Media Relations Specialist at the Michigan Education Association after television news work at KUTV in Salt Lake City and WJBK Fox 2 in Detroit, with a BA from the University of Michigan.

**Item 7.A — Schools of Choice.** State law requires an annual resolution; seats were anticipated for 2011-2012 in grades 9 and 10 at the International Academy East. The proposal covers ten (10) non-resident 10th grade students and an unlimited number of 9th grade students from districts in another county whose intermediate school district is contiguous with the Oakland Intermediate School District boundaries, under Section 105c of the State School Aid Act of 1979 as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996.

**Item 8.A — Infrared wireless microphones.** Invitations to bid went to 21 potential bidders with 9 responses, four of them "No Bid." Scott Bryan, Director of Technology (Technology Resource Center, 4420 Livernois; 248-823-5090), explained that FCC action prohibiting certain radio frequencies forces replacement of free field voice amplification in all lower elementary (K-2) classrooms plus check-out portable systems for upper elementary. Bid #9687 was released July 16, 2010 and opened August 3, 2010. The award to VSC, Inc. totals $74,641.00 from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund, comprising FP-100-R classroom systems $47,190, REDCAT RC-V portable systems $25,056, IR Sensors $895 and shipping $1,500; the recommendation excludes purchase of one each Redmike microphone, controller and cradle. Bid tabulation column totals were 75,253.90, 75,870.00, 78,389.08, 79,240.80 and 69,087.00, for quantities of 110 FP-100-R packages, 27 REDCAT RC-V units and 5 IR sensors; bidders named include Thalner Electronic Labs, Sound Engineering, Troxell Communications, Business Services and VSC, Inc., with No Bids from Broadcast Supply, Advanced Lighting & Sound, B+H Photo and Aves Audio Visual Systems.

**Item 8.B — Wattles sidewalk easement.** Grantors Satyendra N. Basu and Indira Basu of 553 Colebrook, Troy, MI 48083-5110, parcel identification number 88-20-22-252-036, grant a permanent sidewalk easement to the Troy School District for $1.00, covering the South 82.00 feet of the West 33 feet of Lot 58 of "Cloverdale Farms" (Liber 33, Page 13, Oakland County) and part of the NE 1/4 of Section 22, T2N-R11E, north of that plat and west and south of "Hidden Ridge Subdivision" (Liber 173, Pages 5-7). The easement runs with the land, is to be recorded with the Oakland County Register of Deeds with a $20.00 recording fee, and is exempt from state and county transfer tax under MCL 207.505(a) and 207.526(a); it was drafted by Kevin M. Nalu, Esq., Clark Hill PLC, 151 South Old Woodward Avenue, Suite 200, Birmingham, Michigan 48009. The resolution authorizes Superintendent Barbara A. Fowler, Ph.D. to execute it, and certifies adoption at the regular meeting held the 17th day of August, 2010 under the Open Meetings Act, Act 267, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976. Accompanying slides were presented by Mark Rajter.

**Items 10.A-11.A.** Board Committee Membership for 2010-2011 assigns Philippart to the NCA District Team and the Troy Business and Education Roundtable, Edmunds and Hauff to the Safety Committee, Miletti to the Diversity Council, Edmunds/Pochodylo/Underwood to Curriculum, Edmunds/Hauff/Pochodylo to Policy, Fleming/Miletti/Philippart to Superintendent Evaluation, Edmunds to the NSBA National Affiliate Advocacy role, Fleming as MASB Legislative Liaison and to the Senior Advisory Committee, Edmunds and Fleming to the Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence, and Miletti and Underwood to the Wellness Policy Committee. The Board also cancels the September 23-24, 2010 Fall Retreat, schedules a Special Board Workshop for Tuesday, September 28, 2010 at 6:00 p.m. at the Administrative Center, and closes the meeting with a closed session on negotiations under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), by roll call of Pochodylo, Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti and Philippart.
